chapter.num: Ann of the Narzissenkreuz: Act II
chapter.title: Kingdom Through the Looking-Glass

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Déjà vu, perhaps?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Y'know, Paimon thought that she hadn't fully woken up yet... But haven't these things happened before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a...

choices.text: "Fell Shield of Narcissus"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha. That name does fit our adventure up till now, huh?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: This is the center of the world. The castle where the dragon lurks, the tower that imprisons the Princess. Sometimes, it is the lost Ancient City of Ys. Sometimes, Arcadia. At times, it is even golden Hyperborea.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Here, many untrodden realms have been conquered. Here, many heroes have defeated evil dragons.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: This is a place that brims with magic, and I was never really able to understand it. Children could see, through a stone wall, the imaginary griffins that whirl freely in the distant cloud-filled skies.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: These four pools would, in different adventure tales, be the four seas, and sometimes the four cardinal realms of the world.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: I could not understand these things either, but to accompany the children on their adventures, I played all sorts of roles.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are these more of those suddenly-emerging memories?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: ...Yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. Ann, are you alright?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: I don't know. I feel very strange. These memories are so beautiful, but terrifying, too.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Look, there, atop that small fountain. That is the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it really? It looks, uh, kinda cheap.

choices.text: Behold, Paimon, the holy blade!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously? It's just a shabby wooden sword! Still...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: With this sword in hand, Paimon bets the kids sure felt like invincible heroes, ready to take to the skies and do battle with their enemies, huh!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Appropriately-shaped branches and drying poles could also, in the right tale, be the holy blade.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: But she... One day, a certain woman brought several wooden swords for the children to play with, so that the drying poles would stop being used in fights.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...And who was that?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: I do not know. It must have been someone who once lived here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it does seem like the kingdom was once a lively place, with all sorts of people in it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When you think about it like that, the Holy Blade must've been very important.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: A normal sword can cleave flesh, but the Holy Blade can cleave spirit and will.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: As such, even impervious dragons and formless illusions are no match for it.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: If the story of our adventure team is to reach its end, we will need the blade.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it really that powerful? It just looks like a cheap wooden sword...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just take its holiness at face value.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure, if you say so... But it doesn't look like we can reach it right now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's continue exploring. Maybe we'll find some way to break this magical bubble.

choices.text: It's like that time with the Sword of Brilliant Valor...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, okay, Paimon gets it. It is the tale behind the blade and one's belief in it that makes it a holy blade, right?

choices.text: It seems like some sort of seal...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: This is the real "Annapausis."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, why is there a Bubble Formation here too? Was this meant to prevent invaders from kidnapping the Princess?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: ...Yes. That is the case.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, we ran into some enemies earlier. Didn't you say that when Princess Lyris gave you her treasure, the tower stagnated, and even Narcissus could not enter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's... a lot of stuff here that doesn't make sense. What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I don't know either. I never thought about what would happen after we entered the tower.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Also, this place feels very strange. I don't understand. I should never have been here before, but I find myself... recalling, feeling many things.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Do you two not feel it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't either...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Hmmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, do you know what place this is, Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: This was the assembly hall of the Narzissenkreuz Institute. The children would study here normally. I remember now. This was a lovely place. There was no sunlight, but it was always lively here.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: The children were all of different dimensions — some of them as different as the two of you. But here, they would study together, listen to tales of the Hydro Archon... and to tales older still.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dimensions?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I mean that some children were very small, and some were somewhat larger.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey now! Paimon might be small, but she's got a big heart!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—Anyway... What about the Princess? Was she a child, too? Would the children hear stories about her?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I... I don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why does Paimon get the feeling that the story's started drifting away from the Princess ever since we teleported here?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: No, this place must have something to do with her.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: We must be able to find her at the end of this road. She will be happy to see us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you're the local. Paimon trusts you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, finally! The Holy Blade is ours!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It doesn't look like much, but once its powers are awakened, it will become a destructive and invincible weapon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #How is it, {NICKNAME}? Can you feel its power?

choices.text: Uogh! Unlimited power...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Comes not from this blade.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What? C'mon, you had Paimon going there...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come to think of it, Ann, you did mention that the Holy Blade was originally a wooden sword that kids played with...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: That's right. When the young heroes from the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team would pick this sword up, they would become able to defeat all foes in their tale.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Well, let's just take this sword, shall we? Who knows, it might come in handy later — and if not, we can take it as a souvenir.

choices.text: Hmm...
This really is just a wooden toy sword.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this a library?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute. Is it just that Paimon hasn't fully woken up yet, or is it déjà vu? Haven't these things already happened before?

talks.objective: Obtain the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Déjà vu, perhaps?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Y'know, Paimon thought that she hadn't fully woken up yet... But haven't these things happened before?

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Records
dialogues.text: "...Decided to incorporate the institute for raising orphans and the children of criminals into the public welfare system. Considering the ruins of a previous civilization upon which it is situated, it shall be named..."

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Records
dialogues.text: "...The seat of Director was established in honor of the Hydro Archon's great virtue, and has been taken on by a gentle-natured Oceanid. The title of Vice Director is to be taken up by one who displays exceptional moral quality and ability..."

talks.objective: Go on with the help of the Holy Blade's power

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like the path leads downward rather than forward...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is a really long descent...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: It's so creepy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Don't worry, Ann. {NICKNAME}'s really reliable — and really good with a wind glider, too!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But... We don't know what will happen next...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, Princess Lyris waits at the end of this path.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you believe that?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I do.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Yes! That has to be true. Apart from saving the Princess... apart from that one wish, I have nothing at all. I'll do anything to fulfill it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ann...

choices.text: In that case, let's do this for Princess Lyris.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Believe in me and Paimon. Let's go.

choices.text: I am your knight, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We're here to help you, Ann — we're your super reliable helpers!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Believe in us! Also, Paimon thinks that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A real adventure is not only filled with challenges, but also with unknowns. The most important thing is to come back from completing those challenges and unknowns in one piece, and gain something in the end as well. Right?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Yes...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #I believe in you, Knight {NICKNAME}, and in Paimon. You are wise and powerful... and you are also kind people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And ding ding ding, we have a winner! In that case, let's go. "Ad astra abyssosque," as Katheryne always says!

choices.text: I do want to finish this journey, after all.
In that case, let's do this to achieve your goal, Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like the path leads downward rather than forward...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is a really long descent...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: It's so creepy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Don't worry, Ann. {NICKNAME}'s really reliable — and really good with a wind glider, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, Paimon knows. You're worried about what might come afterward, right? Well, don't be!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #A real adventure is not only filled with challenges, but also with unknowns. The most important thing is to come back from completing those challenges and unknowns in one piece, and gain something in the end as well. Isn't that right, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: We've come this far. It would be a shame to give up now.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: True...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #I believe in you, Knight {NICKNAME}, and in Paimon. You are wise and powerful... and you are also kind people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And ding ding ding, we have a winner! In that case, let's go. "Ad astra abyssosque," as Katheryne always says!

choices.text: You did say that Princess Lyris would be just up ahead.

talks.objective: Jump down and reach the end of the story
Jump down and reach the end of the story

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's... kinda... dizzy. There are so many books here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Paimon feels like something should happen right about now...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I feel uneasy too... And I've been... frightened, ever since we came down here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #No need to worry. {NICKNAME} will protect us no matter what, right?

choices.text: Hmm, uh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey! C'mon, you've beaten dragons, {NICKNAME}! Have more faith in yourself!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Yes. I believe in the two of you. I just... don't know what we will encounter later...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll take anything as it comes!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Still, best to be prepared, {NICKNAME}. We might be in for a battle with Narcissus, for all we know!

choices.text: Of course I will.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Someone" wants this tale of adventure to never end.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Eh? What are you on about, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. You know what? Paimon thought that she hadn't fully woken up yet... But haven't these things happened before?

choices.text: But the future of a story that constantly repeats will never come.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Yes...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Princess Lyris waits at the end of this path.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon knows! The last time we were here, you said "On the other hand, we'll be able to leave as long as we find the end of the road," didn't you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Then there must be a way!

choices.text: But we must keep moving forward.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: There will be another adventure, and another, and another one after that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... Even though the Princess is waiting for us at the end of this road, it's just a bunch of connected loops with no real end?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: On the other hand...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll be able to leave as long as we find the end of the road.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh? Do you have an idea, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Any thoughts, Ann?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: I'm sorry. I don't know. I don't know anything about what happens after this...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then let's take stock real quick.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Have you noticed anything, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? You're asking Paimon? Uh, hold on a moment...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: First, the paths here have been connected such that they form a ring, right? In that case, there'd be no getting out...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Except that we were able to get on these paths, so there should be a way off them. There has to be a point from which we can break through.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Next, we saw that... super powerful sword, or something.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Yes, the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It should be a key item in some way...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And why do you think that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it looks like a wooden sword, but it was inside a protective barrier. Would all that trouble be necessary if it wasn't important?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, Paimon thinks that we need to get that sword!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Was there any other notable thing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Paimon can't think of anything at the moment...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But that said, this tile sticks out like a sore thumb, doesn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon didn't just make that one up, by the way! When we passed this way before, it did feel weird how this tile is not connected to the others, and how it has a different pattern.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It could be a trap!

choices.text: That's what I was thinking about as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, guess Paimon's just as smart as you are, eh?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: But you really do have an impressive mind, Paimon. As for me, my head's a mess. I can't get my thoughts straight...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't beat yourself up too much! You're being assaulted by strange memories in this place...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, let's think of how we can get out of this loop based on the stuff we thought of earlier!

choices.text: Good work, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, why are you praising Paimon so seriously all of a sudden? Paimon's not used to this...

choices.text: Let's go over what we know first, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... Why did we meet Narcissus in here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to what we said before, the tower lost its "time" and thus stagnated. As such, no one could open it or enter it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But this space is not within the tower.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We teleported to a different place from the tower.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, that's right! Paimon forgot that that happened... But if that's the case...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But how... No, that can't be true! The Princess should be in the tower. I mean, that was the adventure team's only hope in this dark world...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: If she isn't... Our adventures... their meaning... Al, Petit Chou, and the others...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we did take out the biggest threat to the kingdom, didn't we? That's a good thing, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: ...Yes, you're right, Paimon. Thank you. Thank you both.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anyway, the story's not over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup! Look over there. There's a place we haven't been to before. Maybe we'll find more clues there, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Research
dialogues.text: "... According to the ancient theater and mysterious research hidden here, we believe that the documents and folklore discovered within Petrichor..."

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Research
dialogues.text: "...The research team from Institute of Natural Philosophy holds that..."

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Certificate
dialogues.text: "...The duty will be taken up by Basil Elton, former naval commander. May her steely temper be itself tempered by the family she will establish with these children going forward..."

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Certificate
dialogues.text: "... What's that idiot thinking? Well, whatever. Might as well have some fun post-retirement..."

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Notes
dialogues.text: "...One serving of flour, one of sugar, one of melted butter, two of eggs, a... large amount of milk with which to make foam. Are you kidding me? What exactly is 'a large amount'!? ..."

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Notes
dialogues.text: "...Remember it well this time! 15 minutes at 180 degrees is not the same as 5 at 540!"

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Diary
dialogues.text: "...Linking up with Ingold, Guillotin, and the rest of the old gang will go some way towards solving the dispersion problem. This situation is no place for personal feelings, but what person can lack them completely..."

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Diary
dialogues.text: "...I can only hope that they aren't treating my dear old Sponsian too poorly, or let it rust in the harbor..."

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Diary
dialogues.text: "...And I hope my skills haven't rusted away either."

dialogues.speaker: Rather Aged Diary
dialogues.text: "I hope all goes well. I still want to watch the dough rise to the sounds of play outside the window. I still want to watch them grow into fine adults."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this a bookstore?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What makes you think there'd be secret underground bookstore ruins anywhere in Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute. Is it just that Paimon hasn't fully woken up yet, or is it déjà vu? Haven't these things already happened before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? There's a book here too...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A picture book, huh? It suits you, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! Well, that's because of Paimon's unique sensibility, you know? Picture books just speak to her better!

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: This book... This book gives me a strange feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "A long, long time ago, in a place far, far away, there was once a beautiful and kind Princess named Lyris... and yup, she's our main character!"

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: "'I don't want this name. That's not what you said before.'"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you wanna read it too, Ann? In that case, Paimon's gonna continue. Ahem!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Oh, come on, it's just a story, there's no need to be so fussy. Anyway, a protagonist needs an antagonist... an evil one, at that!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "And our evil antagonist... Well, that's the dragon Narcissus. So evil is he that the peace-loving people tremble at the sound of his name — not that he cares about their feelings, though."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "He sowed destruction across the land with the searing flames he spewed from his mouth. His great wings turned cities to dust and his burning breath reduced nations to ash."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "At last, only the Princess's realm remained safe."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "But because the Princess worked tirelessly to defend her realm, Narcissus's plot to destroy everything could not succeed."

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: "'So, in Narcissus's story, I'm the evil villain?'"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #This is kinda weird. This started like a story book, but it also feels like it isn't... {NICKNAME}, you've got the bigger brain here. You have a look too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Read carefully...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's... kinda... dizzy. There are so many books here...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We already have the Holy Blade.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Eh? What are you on about, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, we really do have it. When did that happen?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. You know what? Paimon thought that she hadn't fully woken up yet... But she definitely remembers that we came here before!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's time to enter the next part of the story.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But... We don't know what will happen next...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, Princess Lyris waits at the end of this path.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you believe that?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I do.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Yes! That has to be true. Apart from saving the Princess... apart from that one wish, I have nothing at all. I'll do anything to fulfill it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ann...

choices.text: In that case, let's do this for Princess Lyris.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Believe in me and Paimon. Let's go.

choices.text: I am your knight, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We're here to help you, Ann — we're your super reliable helpers!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've gotta believe in us. Also, the Princess is waiting!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Yes. I believe in the two of you.

choices.text: I do want to finish this journey, after all.
In that case, let's do this to achieve your goal, Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this a bookstore?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What makes you think there'd be secret underground bookstore ruins anywhere in Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute. Is it just that Paimon hasn't fully woken up yet, or is it déjà vu? Haven't these things already happened before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's... kinda... dizzy. There are so many books here...

choices.text: Is this a library?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: This place... This library has existed since long, long before we arrived.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Their contents seem to be ancient dramas. Children love to read books, but there is much they won't understand, so they will often ask adults to read the stories to them.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: In the books, where there is an evil dragon, there must be heroes who hunt the dragon. If there is a mage, there must be a wandering knight. The Reconquista must come to pass, and the princess must be saved.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: And of course, a chime will sound, and the tale of adventure will come to a halt.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Yet it will not end. There will be another adventure, and another, and another one after that, until the children grow up and leave this place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ann?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Huh? I... Sorry, it felt like memories and feelings suddenly... flooded into my mind. How strange.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Well, as long as you're alright... Paimon thought you might have been bewitched by Narcissus's magic or something!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Urk. That might actually be so!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmmm... Well, what do we do next?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: I'm not sure either...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Whatever the case, let's have a look around.

response.speaker: Paimon
